## Observed Facts

- **Data Scope:** BGL, 1 Jun 2005 to 30 Jun 2005 (end exclusive). The corpus starts 3 Jun 2005 [E1]. In this window there were 1,240,932 Log Entries: INFO 685,088, FATAL 548,475, WARNING 2,568, SEVERE 2,434, ERROR 2,351 [E2].
- **FATAL is concentrated in two weeks.** Weekly FATAL counts were 154,761 for the week of 6 Jun and 380,987 for the week of 13 Jun, against 4,500 and 1,965 in the following two weeks [E4].
- **Two days drive most of it.** Daily FATAL counts were 152,183 on 11 Jun and 344,398 on 14 Jun. Most other days were in the tens to low thousands [E7].
- **Most FATAL entries are tagged KERNEL-side.** The top alert tags were "-" (untagged) 323,323, KERNDTLB 152,659, and KERNSTOR 63,488 [E5]. KERNEL is the component for 1,219,871 of the 1,240,932 Log Entries in the window [E3].
- **One node accounts for a large share.** Node R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 has 152,229 FATAL Log Entries, about 28% of the window's FATAL total. The next-highest node has 128. There are 23,326 distinct FATAL nodes in total [E6].

## Hypotheses

- The June 2005 BGL problem looks like one faulty node (R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01) generating a flood of repeated FATAL KERNEL entries on 11 and 14 Jun, not a broad fleet-wide reliability failure. The rest of the window shows low, steady FATAL activity.
- The most likely component to act on is KERNEL, with the KERNDTLB and KERNSTOR alert tags as the failure types.
- Log volume is not a reliability measure on its own. A single noisy node can inflate the counts.

## Unknowns

- Log Entries are not incidents. The logs cannot tell us how many distinct failures occurred, so do not report "X incidents" to leadership.
- The logs cannot establish downtime, job failures, lost compute, customer or user impact, or cost. None of these can be stated from this data.
- I have not confirmed that KERNDTLB and KERNSTOR entries are all from the same node. Node and alert-tag were checked separately.
- I have not checked whether the spike was a repeated message from one hardware fault or many separate faults. A sample of the raw messages would settle that.
- Whether the node was repaired or removed is not in the logs.

## Next Step

Pull a sample of the raw KERNDTLB FATAL messages from 11 and 14 Jun 2005 to confirm they are repeats from node R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01, then report to leadership the frequency and the affected component (KERNEL) and node. For the headline, say "548,475 FATAL Log Entries in June 2005, about 28% from one node, concentrated on 11 and 14 June," and avoid any claim about impact.
